appraisal_events.evidence: tous ceux qui cherchaient à savoir qui était dans la salle sentaient se relever dans leur cœur le trône légitime de la beauté... c'était la forme d'un corps et d'un visage délicieux que la princesse apposait à l'angle de sa loge, montrant par là que la beauté peut être la plus noble des signatures.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator sharply elevates the princesse de Guermantes as the sole genuine embodiment of aristocratic beauty in the theater, contrasting her authentic charm with the merely conventional 'aristocratic' ugliness of other titled women, and effectively overriding the neighbor's dismissive mockery of her display as pretentious.

appraisal_events.evidence: Personne n'excitait en moi autant d'envie que lui, à cause de l'habitude qu'il avait l'air d'avoir de cette baignoire et de l'indifférence avec laquelle il laissait la princesse lui tendre des bonbons; elle jetait alors sur lui un regard de ses beaux yeux...
appraisal_events.explanation: Palancy is elevated in the narrator's eyes through his apparent habitual intimacy with the princesse's box and the special, jewel-eyed attention she directs at him, provoking open envy despite his outwardly comic, fish-like torpor.

status_effects.explanation: She is framed as the sole authentic embodiment of aristocratic beauty and legitimacy, decisively outranking other titled women identified only by conventional features, and this stands even against an onlooker's mocking dismissal.

His apparent habitual familiarity with the princesse's box and her personal, attentive gaze toward him mark him as enviably intimate with her circle, elevating his local standing despite his outwardly inert demeanor.

ambiguities: The passage refers to the princesse once as 'Mme de Guermantes'; this is resolved here as the princesse de Guermantes-Bavière (not the duchesse) based on the accompanying reference to her palaces in Munich and Paris.
The neighbor's 'marquis de Ganançay' appears to be a mishearing of 'marquis de Palancy', referring to the same 'gros monsieur en frac'; treated as one entity in this annotation.
